_readme: Self-learning substrate. `observations` is the only ground truth -- append-only, never edited in place. `parameters` holds each tunable's STATE (default/shadow/active/escalated) and change history; the numeric value itself is DERIVED from observations on every read via smith_learning.evaluate(), never cached here as authoritative. `lessons` is corrections, decisions not to re-litigate, and dead ends -- read this before proposing a fix that sounds familiar, it may already be lesson #1.

phase4.readiness.note: Not a calibrated value -- a readiness counter. Phase 4 (conviction WEIGHTS calibration) stays deliberately unbuilt until this reaches 100 scored proposals, per explicit user decision 2026-08-25. See learn-lessons for the full context.

lessons.text: Revealed-preference size effect (acted-on median $700 vs ignored $360) evaporated under a within-month control: July acted $705 vs ignored $700, August $325 vs $300 -- size does not predict whether the user acts. The apparent effect was pure time-confounding (8/9 acted-on rows are July, 33/37 ignored rows are August). Do not re-derive or auto-apply a sizing correction from pooled acted-vs-ignored size comparisons; always split by period first.

cmd_journal prices tickers only from the current run's holdings.json, so an exited ticker can never be priced and its journal entry stays verdict:open forever. This creates survivorship bias in every bucket hit rate -- entries that fail to score are disproportionately the ones that went wrong enough to get stopped out. Fix (Phase 1): give cmd_journal an injected --prices-json like cmd_score/cmd_stops already have.

The tier-cliff bug: CONVICTION_TIERS' step-function pct field, looked up directly, meant two candidates one point apart on either side of a tier boundary (e.g. score 44 vs 46 across the 45pt low/medium line) got a 2x size difference for a 1-point difference in conviction. WDC reached the highest evidence tier (primary verification) and its size did not move at all because it stayed on the low side of the 45pt line. Fixed same-day by splitting tier LABEL (still discrete, for display) from tier PCT (now piecewise-linear interpolation via TIER_PCT_ANCHORS).

smith_core.load_json(path, default=X)'s missing-file branch only returns X when X is truthy-checked as 'is not None' -- so calling with default=None (indistinguishable from omitting it) always raises FileNotFoundError instead of returning None. Bit smith_memory.py's new standalone-journal compaction pass and smith_learning.py's own load_store during this session. Workaround used both times: pass default={} and test emptiness, not default=None + is None. Root cause in smith_core.py:307-313 is unfixed -- flagged here so a future session doesn't waste time rediscovering the same trap, and can consider fixing load_json itself (risk: unclear if any existing caller relies on the raise-on-explicit-None behavior).

Corrects an earlier same-day guess (see the lesson about cmd_journal survivorship bias): the direction of the bias was assumed to be optimistic (excluded losers inflate hit rates). VERIFIED WRONG on first real backfill of 16 exited tickers / 14 newly-scoreable entries: TARGET GAP moved UP 23.1%->36.8% (n=13->19) because the excluded entries were disproportionately WINNERS this time (IREN +10.8%, LITE +15.2%, ORCL +17.8% x2, DLR +4.5%), while MOMENTUM+VOLUME stayed flat at 0% (n=7->11) with no direction change. The real defect is that exclusion itself is non-random -- an exited name correlates with volatile price action in EITHER direction (that volatility is often why it triggered a stop), not uniformly bad. Do not assume a direction for this bias when reasoning about it in future work; the fix (inject exited-ticker prices) is correct, the assumed mechanism was not.

First real shadow-trigger hit rates now exist (trigger_journal.json scored for the first time, 2026-08-25): laggard_rotation 0% (n=3) -- every laggard-rotation candidate flagged so far failed to catch up; scale_out_ladder 100% (n=5) -- every scale-out trim so far was followed by the price falling, validating the trim. profit_ratchet stays permanently n/a by design (a stop-management action, not a directional price bet). derisk_journal's narrow_stretch queue_state is 0% (n=3) -- none of the three names flagged as fragile/stretched have underperformed since. All four n are far below any reasonable promotion gate (want n>=20-30 before treating a shadow trigger's hit rate as real) -- these are early reads to watch, not yet a basis for promoting anything from shadow to live.

Stop-distance calibration read (Phase 3, n=140 scored stops): overall 48.8%, cascade cohort 50.0% (n=29), deliberate cohort 54.2% (n=79) -- all within +/-10pp of a coin flip, no clear signal to widen or tighten stop_distance_pct in either cohort at current sample size. This CORRECTS a stale SKILL.md claim of '75% deliberate / 25% cascade' that was based on an n=6 snapshot; that divergence did not survive the sample growing to n=108 across the two real cohorts. The 'unknown' cohort (n=32, missing/unparseable fill_time_utc) reads 34.5%, below the coin-flip band, but this cohort's classification is itself data-quality-confounded (a missing timestamp is not a real cascade/deliberate signal) so this reading should not be treated as a genuine finding about stop behavior. Per-ATR-tier calibration (as opposed to cascade/deliberate) is not currently possible -- stops_analysis.json rows carry no ATR-at-fill. No change to policy.json's stop_loss_framework is warranted or was made; this is an escalation-only, no-action-indicated finding.

Phase 4 (conviction WEIGHTS calibration -- smith_conviction.py's thesis/catalyst/trend/valuation/earnings/technical/corroboration weights) is EXPLICITLY DEFERRED by user decision on 2026-08-25, not just blocked by data. Currently 8 of the ~100 scored proposals needed to attribute outcome to component. Do not build Phase 4's calibration logic or start wiring WEIGHTS to learning.json until proposals.json's scored count (outcome_verdict present) reaches 100 -- check with 'smith_math.py score' + counting outcome_verdict, same method used here. When it does, the user wants Phase 4 executed then, not skipped. Until then this is a known, deliberate pause, not a forgotten task.
lessons.evidence: proposals.json: 8/159 scored as of 2026-08-25; plans/clever-watching-hinton.md Phase 4
